notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity and reliability. Kestrel runs low-latency user-facing chat for traders (p99 target 60-120ms per token), and a reranking pipeline for search results (throughput lanes: 5k qps batch reranker during market open). Primary concerns: guaranteed sustained throughput during spikes, deterministic latency SLOs, and a resilient fallback strategy if Dedicated pool saturates.

POC/Technical requirements: 
- Throughput guarantees: need example sizing showing reserved GPU counts for 3 sustained load profiles (baseline 2k qps, peak 7k qps, flash 12k qps) and expected token/sec per GPU for 8-bit quantized models.
- Latency SLOs: insist on p95 and p99 per-route SLOs; p99 for chat must be <= 200ms (prefer 120ms). Want rollback credits if SLO breaches exceed 0.5% of request volume.
- Reserved GPU planning: want deterministic headroom math + recommended burst policy (autoscale + reserved burst buckets). Ask for sample contract language tying reserved capacity to monthly commit and step-up windows.
- SLA negotiations: legal asked to include cross-region failover timelines (RTO), model-variant fallback commitments, and defined credit formula for missed throughput.

Reliability & fallback design preferences discussed: 
- Cross-region failover: Kestrel requires active-warm pair strategy: traffic routed primary region; on detection of degradation, automatic cutover to warm region within configured RTO (<= 3 minutes); warm region must maintain model cache priming to avoid cold KV-cache penalties. Explicit requirement to support regional KV cache pre-warming and snapshot restore.
- Model-variant fallback: prefer deterministic fallback chain: primary full-precision model -> quantized variant -> smaller model family -> queued degraded-mode with degraded-response headers. Must preserve semantic fidelity for critical financial queries. Want tooling to simulate saturations and validate fallback correctness (golden prompt sets + eval harness).
- Graceful degradation rules: hard vs soft limits per route, queueing policy when pool saturated, throttling headers to caller, circuit-breaker metrics visible in Console.

Open action items: 
- AE/SE to provide reserved GPU sizing report and cost delta for burst policy (deliver by 2026-03-17).
- Engineering to produce runbook draft for cross-region failover and KV cache priming steps (link: drive:/kestrel/architecture/cross-region-failover-draft.md).
- Legal to propose SLA credit calc (Kestrel legal expects simple % uptime + throughput shortfall credits).
- Kestrel to provide golden prompt set for fallback validation (security wants samples sanitized).

Quotes / meeting notes: 
- From Head of Platform: "If we lose our primary region during market open, every millisecond costs revenue — need hard guarantees and a tested playbook."
- SRE: "We can't accept a multi-minute cold start on cache restore. Warm pools + pre-warm snapshots are necessary."

Risks called out: 
- Model fidelity drift when falling back to quantized or smaller variants; requires eval gating and rollback trigger thresholds.
- Pricing complexity around burst capacity and crediting language (ops vs commercial alignment needed).

Stubs/refs: pricing deck, security FAQ, inbound Fireflies transcripts attached. Jira tickets opened for runbook draft (INF-3421) and security clarifications (SEC-1282).
